nominees.name: Edward Witten
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

subfield: Quantum gravity and quantum field theory (holography)
motivation: In 1997 Maldacena proposed that string theory in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a conformal gauge theory on its boundary. Together with Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov, and independently Witten, who gave the precise dictionary linking bulk fields to boundary correlators, this established holography as a concrete, calculable framework. The correspondence gives a non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity, shows that black hole evaporation is unitary, and turns hard strong-coupling problems into tractable geometric ones. It has changed how physicists think about spacetime itself: entanglement entropy, quantum error correction and complexity are now understood as ingredients of emergent geometry. Its methods are widely used in nuclear physics (quark-gluon plasma viscosity), condensed matter (strange metals, quantum criticality) and quantum information, and are increasingly tested in analogue and quantum-simulation experiments. Few theoretical ideas of the last half-century have been taken up so broadly across physics.
